page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon CPU with 4 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core operating at 2.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Crucially, this instance includes a bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. General compute performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU evaluations all falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth and data compression tasks, such as bzip3 decompression, also register in the weak to poor categories. However, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers exceptional performance for artificial intelligence workloads. LLM inference speeds for both small (135M) and medium (7B) models reach top-tier status, placing in the top 10% for both prompt processing and text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-4 offers a specialized entry point for GPU-accelerated computing without the overhead of larger multi-GPU configurations. While the modest CPU and memory resources represent a bottleneck for general-purpose computing or heavy data processing, the instance provides high resource density for targeted graphics and machine learning tasks. This server is optimized for workloads such as low-latency LLM inference, small-to-medium scale AI model serving, and GPU-accelerated graphics rendering, rather than database operations or CPU-heavy compilation.
